gettysburg-address: Abraham Lincoln spoke for barely two minutes at the dedication of a soldiers’ cemetery in Gettysburg, Pennsylvania, on November 19, 1863. He honored the Union dead of the Civil War’s bloodiest battle and urged the living to finish the work of preserving a nation ‘conceived in liberty.’ Few speeches have been memorized so widely; its closing promise of ‘government of the people, by the people, for the people’ still echoes today.
the-theology-of-holiness: Quaker minister Dougan Clark sets out the doctrine of holiness — the belief that believers can be cleansed from sin in this life — with careful scriptural argument. Written for the holiness movement of the late 1800s, the book explains its teachings plainly and devoutly. An important window into a powerful current of American religious life.
metlakahtla-and-the-north-pacific-missio: Eugene Stock tells the remarkable story of Metlakahtla — William Duncan's Christian Indigenous community on British Columbia's north coast. Mission history with all its triumphs, tensions, and controversies. A fascinating chapter of the Pacific Northwest. The story raises enduring questions about faith, culture, and colonial power.
dr-heidenhoff-s-process: Edward Bellamy — of Looking Backward fame — imagines Dr. Heidenhoff's process, a treatment that wipes guilty memories clean. His hero tests it with strange results. A clever, haunting early work of science fiction. Can science wipe away a guilty past? Bellamy's strange, clever tale asks the question with chilling effect.
the-hour-glass: W. B. Yeats' Hour Glass — his verse morality play of the wise man, the fool, and the angels — shows the great poet as a dramatist of ideas. Irish myth and modern doubt contend in symbolic beauty. Yeats' theater at its most haunting.
tales-of-the-wilderness: Boris Pilniak's Tales of the Wilderness — stark stories of revolutionary Russia's wild places and wilder men — show his savage, lyrical power. The author's strange genius burns in every page. Unforgettable and unsettling Soviet literature. Snow, blood, and strange faiths haunt his powerful stories.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abbess: This 1913 Catholic reference piece on the abbess — the head of a house of nuns — sets out her rights and duties in plain church law. Thomas Oestereich writes it up with care. Hilda of Whitby and Hildegard show what abbesses could be.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-abyss: A 1913 entry on the abyss — the deep of Genesis and the pit of Revelation. Anthony Maas gathers the scriptural senses. Waters below and darkness beneath meet here. A short, weighty word study. The Vulgate's abyssus shaped a thousand sermons. Preachers loved its dark and dreadful sound.
